comment: 61 pages, 4 figures in the main text; Supplementary Information included. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043086
summary: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

title: Quantum Robustness via Sandwiched Rényi Divergences
summary: If a quantum state is known only approximately, how much can the expectation of an observable change? We answer with the worst-case expectation over all states within a sandwiched Rényi divergence budget of a reference state, for every order $α\in [1/2,\infty]$. Convex duality gives this value as a one-dimensional optimization over a sandwiched Schatten norm, running from a fidelity risk at $α= 1/2$, through the entropic risk at $α= 1$, to a quantum conditional value-at-risk at $α= \infty$. The main result is a classicalization theorem: the quantum problem coincides with the classical one for a probability measure $ω_α$ on the spectral interval of the observable, constructed from Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure and given by Stahl's theorem at $α= 1$. The Hoeffding, Bernstein and Markov--Krein bounds of classical probability thereby apply to the quantum problem, and yield Pinsker-type inequalities with Bernstein-type refinements. The measure $ω_α$ is the Born measure only at $α= 1/2$; for $α> 1/2$, noncommutativity of the observable with the state strictly lowers its variance below the Born variance, and with it every variance-sensitive bound: a quantum deflation.

title: Vacuum energy interacting with dark matter and dark radiation: alleviating the $H_0$-$S_8$ seesaw
summary: Extensions of $Λ$CDM that raise $H_0$ with additional energy before recombination, such as dark radiation and early dark energy (EDE), also raise $S_8$. We study whether a late-time energy exchange between the vacuum and the dark sector can offset this increase. The coupling rate scales as $\bar m H^α$ and is negligible before recombination for $α\le -2$; the energy is transferred along the four-velocity of geodesic cold dark matter, so the dark matter produced by the vacuum carries no density perturbation and slows the growth of structure. We add the exchange to dark radiation ($\bar m\tildeΛ$CDM) and to a one-parameter EDE model ($\bar m$EDE), and constrain the models with Planck 2018, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ data (CBS), and with the SH0ES calibration added (CBSH) to test the exchange when $H_0$ is held at a high value. For CBS the posteriors favour an energy flow from the vacuum into dark matter at 1.8-2.7$σ$, and the exchange lowers $S_8$ by 0.02-0.08 but does not raise $H_0$: $\bar m\tildeΛ$CDM gives $H_0 = 68.83 \pm 0.91$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, 3.1$σ$ below SH0ES. For CBSH the exchange removes the increase of $S_8$ caused by dark radiation, giving $S_8 = 0.800 \pm 0.016$ at $H_0 = 71.34 \pm 0.70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, and about a third of that caused by EDE for $α= -2$, with the coupling at 1.1-2.0$σ$. The reduction of $S_8$ is concentrated at $z \lesssim 0.3$: at the redshifts probed by KiDS-Legacy the lensing amplitude decreases by only 1-2%, the shear $χ^2$ of the dark-radiation models changes by less than 3, and the exchange reduces but does not remove the excess shear $χ^2$ of EDE. A late-time exchange can therefore offset part of the $S_8$ increase of early-time solutions, but it does not ease the Hubble tension, and current data do not require it.

title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
summary: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2Ω_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

title: In-Band Boundary Resonances from Coalescing Zero-Group-Velocity Points
summary: Boundary states generally reside in band gaps, whereas in-band confinement typically requires exact decoupling from propagating modes. We demonstrate an alternative mechanism in reciprocal, topologically trivial Hermitian lattices arising from the coalescence of two zero-group-velocity (ZGV) points. At coalescence, the group velocity and inverse effective mass vanish simultaneously, and the corresponding Bloch root acquires higher multiplicity. The coalesced root remains propagating, whereas nearby root splitting yields weakly evanescent channels that, together with a bulk-matched termination, generate a boundary-weighted resonance within the propagating spectrum. The mechanism is realized analytically in a two-leg ladder model through the coalescence of time-reversal-related ZGVs and extends to distinct ZGVs produced by longer-range interactions. Finite-size scaling distinguishes the resulting resonance from extended and defect-bound states. Scanning laser Doppler vibrometry on a 3D-printed elastic ladder reveals boundary enhancement in a nearly flat band region, consistent with operation slightly below criticality. ZGV coalescence thus provides a bulk framework for in-band boundary resonances in reciprocal Hermitian lattices.

title: Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms
summary: We propose a unified architecture for two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum processors which allows the implementation of the complete set of two-qubit gates. Our approach rests on a single resource that unlocks the entire gate set: an XXZ interaction with tunable anisotropy, combined only with single-qubit operations. We introduce a Rydberg-atom realization of the tunable XXZ interaction and combine it with optimally controlled global microwave pulses to implement the B, QFT, iSWAP, and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates, as well as a continuous gate family interpolating from CZ to iSWAP via the B gate. This work allows the implementation of any two-qubit gate natively in neutral-atom platforms, enabling flexible switching between instruction sets to reduce circuit depth and compilation overhead in quantum algorithm implementation.

title: Work needed to lift a mass in Schwarzschild spacetime
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in European Journal of Physics
summary: We determine the work needed to lift a mass from $r_2$ to $r_1$ in Schwarzschild spacetime in three ways. First we use a winch and a light rope. Then we use a photon collision. Finally we let the mass decay into photons and reconstruct it at the higher radius. All three methods give the same local work at $r_1$, $W_1=mc^2[1-N(r_2)/N(r_1)]$, where $N(r)=\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$. Thus, independently of $r_1$, the work tends to $mc^2$ as $r_2$ approaches the horizon. The rope example also gives a useful general-relativistic version of a simple machine: a rope in equilibrium need not have equal local forces at its two ends. The redshift factor plays the role of the lever arm. For a real rope the energy conditions prevent the tension from decreasing with height, so this lever advantage is confined to the idealization. The examples are intended as teaching material for undergraduate relativity courses.

title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
summary: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

title: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2$M$-WS$_2$
summary: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2$M$-WS$_2$. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2$M$-K$_x$WS$_2$ and find that K$^+$ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K$^+$ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2$M$-WS$_2$ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K$^+$ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2$M$-WS$_2$. A six-hour treatment with acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio ($\overline{RRR}$). Residual K$^+$, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on $\overline{RRR}$. Treatments yielding crystals with $\overline{RRR}$ below this bound did not always afford 2$M$-WS$_2$; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
summary:
For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations.
  We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

title: The shape and velocity of black hole coronas
summary: The first highly significant detection of the polarization of the X-rays from the Black Hole X-ray Binary Cygnus X-1 revealed surprisingly strong polarization parallel to its radio jet. The observation is now commonly interpreted as resulting from the Comptonization of some lower frequency seed photons in a laterally extended corona. The emitting plasma is likely moving along the jet axis with a sizable fraction beta of the speed of light, amplifying the polarization degree. In this letter we address the question of how laterally extended the corona actually needs to be to account for the observations, and we calculate the required outflow velocities of velocity-stratified coronas as a function of the stationary-frame aspect ratio h=H/2R of cylindrical coronas of height H and radius R. We find that models with h lesser equal 0.8 and beta=0.5-0.9 at the top of the corona can give both the observed photon index of Gamma=1.6 and the observed 4% polarization parallel to the symmetry axis. We do not find suitable solutions for larger h. Given the constraints on h, we discuss the likely size of the corona, emphasizing that compact coronas close to the black hole are preferred as they can tap more efficiently into the gravitational energy and the rotational energy of the black hole, and are less exposed to their own emission reprocessed in the optically thick portion of the accretion flow.

title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
summary: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
summary: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

title: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight
summary: We complete a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) in the mathematical framework of Half-Sided Translations and Modular Inclusions (HST/HSMI) removing an assumption that applied to previous proofs. Here we establish a theorem, which when translated to a physical setting implies that the relative entropy comparing the state of fields outside a stationary black hole with a Hartle-Hawking (HH) state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. Previous proofs only applied when a purification with finite null energy was available. We also obtain a QNEC generalization in which the HH Hilbert space is replaced with one based on a weight which is plausibly of relevance to evaporating black holes in flat space.

title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
comment: 17 pages; comments and feedbacks are welcome
summary: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4π\bmod 1/2π$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

title: Superconductivity and Polar Metallicity in Atomically Thin Nitride Superlattices
summary: The integration of polar and superconducting materials in the atomically thin limit typically results in a competition that suppresses the superconducting order. Here, we challenge this conventional view by employing first-principles calculations to investigate 1:1 superlattices composed of alternating atomically thin layers of TiN/AlN and δ-NbN/AlN. Contrary to the expectation that dense insulating barriers would quench superconductivity, we find that the polar interface can coexist with a superconducting state. We observe that the transition temperature (Tc) of TiN is enhanced by nearly 2 K over its bulk value, while δ-NbN maintains a relatively high Tc exceeding 20 K. We demonstrate that this resilience arises from the formation of a polar metal, where the strong internal electric fields of the AlN layers are partially screened by a charge redistribution within the nitride layers. This screening mechanism, along with the geometric confinement, creates a quasi-two-dimensional electronic environment, establishing these superlattices as a novel platform for exploring the coexistence of structural inversion-symmetry breaking and superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit.

title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
summary: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,δ_B,ε_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $δ_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $ε_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $ι_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,δ_{O_q},ε_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $δ_{O_q}$ (resp. $ι_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $ε_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $δ_{O_q}$ and $ι_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Przeździecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.

title: Einstein--Yang--Mills Plane Waves: Uniqueness and an Exact Curvature Double Copy
summary: Coleman found plane waves of Yang--Mills theory that are genuinely non-abelian in four dimensions and yet obey linear field equations, and Güven showed that they remain exact when gravity is included. We study these waves in $D$ dimensions. Coleman's profile, which is linear in the transverse coordinates, is singled out twice: up to gauge, it is the only profile with bounded energy density, and the only one for which the full Riemann tensor equals the color-contracted square of the Yang--Mills field strength that sources it. In anti-de Sitter space, we construct a closed-form family for every $D\geq4$; there, the full Riemann tensor cannot equal this color square. Waves whose transverse space is a sphere are always singular. In quadratic and Gauss--Bonnet gravity, a hyperbolic transverse space avoids this only if the waves defocus light or the higher-curvature terms become comparable to the Einstein term. All solutions extend, with changed coefficients, to generic gravity and gauge theories.

title: A geometrical approach for obtaining exact analytical solutions for a scalar field in a one-dimensional dynamical cavity
summary: The dynamical Casimir effect was first predicted by G. T. Moore in 1969, who considered a real scalar field inside a cavity with a moving mirror in ($1+1$)D, satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. However, its application has always been done through numerical calculations, and their approach has therefore long been regarded solely as a numerical method. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation. We obtain original exact analytical solutions for an expanding cavity with a uniformly moving mirror, a contracting cavity with a mirror that approaches the static one asymptotically, and, in addition, we recover the first analytical solution to the Moore equation for a resonant mirror motion, originally obtained by Law in 1994. Moreover, we extend the Cole-Schieve approach, showing that exact solutions can be constructed from any spacetime region where the Moore function has already been determined. We show that this extended geometrical approach allows us to expand the set of known analytical solutions to the Moore equation from the few classes of motion reported in the literature to an infinite set, as it enables the treatment of new classes of laws of motion obtained by combining those presented here with each other as well as with previously known classes of trajectories.

title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
summary: Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10^10 s^-1, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
summary: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.

title: Projective symmetries and differential recursions for the large-$N$ Gross--Witten--Wadia and one-dimensional QCD matrix models
summary: We compare the fixed-charge planar Gross--Witten--Wadia (GWW) model with source-free one-dimensional QCD at large $N$ and $N_f/N$ fixed. In both models the resolvent and one-cut condition give an algebraic equation for a derivative of the free energy: a quartic for GWW and a sextic for QCD. Finite-$N$ Toeplitz determinants independently check the selected QCD branch. Signed permutations of homogeneous parameter triples realize $S_4$; the resulting action on the algebraic branches and operator labels gives a common projective description of the two models. For QCD, the sextic yields a differential recurrence linking small-charge rows two apart. The same second-order PDE gives a finite-width column recursion that reconstructs the coefficient pyramid from its GWW boundary. A distinct boundary, obtained from the first resummed coefficient, is the Narayana triangle. A formally collapsed slice counts decorated bipartite plane trees and admits an exact symmetric product formula. The many-flavor scaling reduces the sextic to the quartic and retains transverse projective data: the QCD divided-difference triple coalesces at this boundary, whereas the limiting quartic satisfies the full standard GWW third-order system. We distinguish algebraic degree, mixed differential order, and fixed-parameter ordinary differential order throughout.

title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
summary: Electronic band structures govern how crystals conduct electrons and absorb light. Density-functional theory (DFT) computes them through costly self-consistent iterations, while existing machine-learning models either predict isolated scalar properties or output Hamiltonians that still require DFT solvers. Here we present EpNet, a learned empirical pseudopotential for crystals spanning 63 elements across the \textit{s}, \textit{p} and \textit{d} blocks. An equivariant neural network builds its Hamiltonian from physics-motivated local potentials and nonlocal projectors. Trained solely on band energies, EpNet predicts complete band structures directly from atomic coordinates. On unseen chemical systems, its median errors are \winAll\ eV for band energies and \gapAll\ eV for band gaps. On 600,000 structures from an independent database, its band-gap errors are overall less than half those of existing models, at about 1\% of DFT cost. EpNet thus enables fast screening of electronic properties for materials discovery and electronic-structure simulations of large systems.

title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Supplemental Material (8 pages) included. Code and data: https://github.com/prashantstar123/urca-neutrino-reabsorption
summary: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordström Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity
summary: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordström black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenböck invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordström background.

title: Spin Conductivity: Insight From Perturbation Theory
summary: The investigation on the spin conductivity has now been blooming in burgeoning altermagnetic materials. Here, an alternative and elementary derivation for the spin conductivity expression is presented. This is done within the context of perturbation theory. It indicates that our derived expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-even ($\mathcal{T}$ for time reversal) spin conductivity agrees exactly with those derived from the Kubo linear response theory and quantum kinetic theory. In addition, the expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-odd spin conductivity in the clean limit is exactly consistent with those presented previously. We show that the $\mathcal{T}$-odd ($\mathcal{T}$-even) spin conductivity arises from the contribution of zeroth-order (first-order) wave function correction. Our work provides some physical insight into the spin conductivity from the perturbation theory and shines more light on the charge-to-spin conversion mechanism in magnetic materials.

title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
summary: We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.

title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, conference proceedings for ICHEP 2026, on behalf of the Belle II Collaboration
summary: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\toηh^+$, $D\toππ$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\toπ^+π^-π^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $Ξ_c^+\toΣ^+h^+h^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=π,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $ηh^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\toππ$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.

title: Odd Darcy Law: Odd Viscosity and Edge Currents in Porous Media
summary: We derive and numerically validate an odd Darcy law for chiral active fluids in porous media, in which an antisymmetric permeability tensor induces a flow transverse to the applied pressure gradient. We identify two distinct mechanisms leading to this odd response: odd viscosity in the fluid or the nonlinear coupling of edge currents to inertia. We then show how the transverse transport depends on porosity, boundary friction, and chirality.

title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.

title: Naturalness in the Past from a Time-Dependent Supersymmetry Scale
summary: We consider the possibility that electroweak naturalness may be epoch dependent. In no-scale supergravity, a rolling quintessence modulus can control the supersymmetry-breaking scale, allowing superpartners to be much lighter in the early universe while remaining heavy today. Fifth-force and varying-constant effects can be suppressed via correlated modular weights in the visible-sector Kähler metric and modulus-dependent superpotential Yukawa couplings, while radiative stability of the quintessence potential requires additional tuning of the field-dependent vacuum energy. The resulting effective theory has distinctive implications for early-universe phase transitions, relic abundances, and gravitational waves.

title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
summary: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. Once decoupled from matter, the photons evolve under the free cavity Hamiltonian while retaining correlations acquired in the interacting gas. Interference between cavity modes produces oscillations in the photon density, while resonant pair correlations persist after interaction removal and distinguish the resulting photon state from a quadratic thermal state with the same one-body density matrix.

title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
summary: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Padé methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.

title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
summary: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.

title: Electron cooling mediated by transverse optical phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$
summary: Soft transverse optical (TO) phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$ couple to electrons through the polarization field, quadratically in the paraelectric phase and, additionally, linearly in the polar phase due to the onset of spontaneous polarization. We investigate heat flow between a three-dimensional electron gas and soft TO phonons. For two-TO-phonon scattering, the heat flow of hot electrons crosses over from $T^5$ to $T^3$ at the Bloch-Gruneisen temperature. In the polar phase, an additional one-TO-phonon channel emerges, yielding a softer temperature dependence of the heat flow, $T^3$ at low and $T$ at high temperatures, with the spectral weight set by the spontaneous polarization. This channel may dominate at low temperatures and leads to a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the heat flow in the vicinity of the polar transition.

title: Effective Time Advance of Quantum Clocks under Postselection
summary: In the familiar twin paradox, the traveling twin ages less than the one who stays behind as a consequence of relativistic time dilation. Here, we show that quantum postselection can effectively reverse this outcome. Using an analytically solvable quantum clock model, we demonstrate that postselection of the center-of-mass motion produces an effective time advance through anomalous weak values, even though every individual motional branch undergoes ordinary time dilation. We extend this analysis to a weak gravitational field and show that an effective time advance can arise even for simple coherent states of the quantum clock motion. We further illustrate this effect using a hydrogen-like atom, revealing how it manifests itself in the atomic wavefunction. Our results demonstrate that quantum interference and postselection can produce an effective time advance beyond conventional relativistic time dilation.

title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
summary: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
summary: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

title: On Thermodynamic Role of the Gauss-Bonnet Topological Term
summary: We revisit the thermodynamic implications of the Gauss-Bonnet topological term in four spacetime dimensions. It has been previously claimed in the literature that this term, although it does not modify the equations of motion, shifts the black hole entropy by a contribution proportional to the Euler characteristic of the horizon. We argue that this conclusion is sensitive to the choice of the boundary action on the horizon. We then identify a choice for which the Wald entropy expression naturally reproduces the Jacobson-Myers entropy, even for non-stationary black holes. We also show that there are no further contributions to conserved quantities from smooth outer boundaries, regardless of the choice of boundary conditions there and of the asymptotic behaviour of the spacetime. Moreover, we demonstrate that the topological Gauss-Bonnet term changes the critical temperature of the Hawking-Page phase transition, opening, in principle, a way for detecting its presence in the gravitational action. In fact, for a positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant, we observe a zeroth-order Hawking phase transition at high temperatures and pressures. While our discussion focuses on the case of the Gauss-Bonnet term in 4D, the results are more general and qualitatively apply to other Lovelock Lagrangians in their respective critical dimensions.

title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
summary: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Padé methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.

title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$
summary: We study the effect of electron correlation ($U$) and hydrostatic pressure on the electronic properties of double perovskites La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$ for $x$ = 0, 0.5, and 1, using first-principles electronic structure calculations within density functional theory (DFT). At ambient pressure, we systematically vary the electron correlation, i.e., on-site Coulomb interaction to study its effect on band gap and structural parameters. Increasing the value of $U$ enhances the band gap of all three compositions while producing only a slight variation in structural parameters. The effect of hydrostatic pressure is also studied for the same compositions. The estimated band gap values at ambient pressure closes at approximately 39, 42, and 53 GPa for $x$ = 0 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), 0.5 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), and 1 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 4 eV), respectively, indicating pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transitions. These results show that electron correlation stabilises the insulating state, whereas hydrostatic pressure favours the metallic state by closing the band gap. These findings highlight the tunability of correlated oxides through electron correlations and pressure, offering insights for materials design.

title: Boundary Formula for Volume Response of Entanglement Wedge Polygons
summary: The vacuum volume of an entanglement wedge polygon is topological. We determine its semiclassical quadratic response to time-symmetric coherent scalar matter in AdS$_3$. A contrast of six interval entropies measures a nonnegatively weighted energy integral, whereas volume depends on the unweighted integral. For negative mass squared above the stability bound, perturbations with the same quadratic coefficient of global energy can match all six vacuum entropies through second order yet have opposite volume responses. A continuum of narrowing quartets reconstructs the volume response with controlled noise. An independent CFT calculation for a dimension-$3/2$ primary reproduces an exact polygon edge formula.

title: Pentagon Functions for Two-Loop Leading-Colour $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ Amplitudes with a Light-Quark Loop
summary: We present a basis of special functions and an efficient numerical implementation for the planar two-loop master integrals that enter the leading-colour amplitudes for $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ with a closed light-quark loop. We provide analytic results for the special functions at transcendental weight one and two in terms of logarithms and dilogarithms, while higher weights are evaluated as one-fold integrals. We focus on the nested roots that arise, studying their analytic structure on the physical region and constructing numerically stable representations of letters and $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms that involve them. We find that a number of $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms have an antiderivative that cannot be represented by a single logarithm over the physical region and tackle them numerically with adaptive Chebyshev approximation. We implement the functions in \texttt{C++} as an extension of the \texttt{PentagonFunctions++} library. We study the performance of our implementation over physical phase-space points and find that the evaluation is accurate and fast enough for phenomenological application. This provides an important building block for NNLO studies of $t\bar{t}H$ production at the LHC.

title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
summary: As ferroelectric devices approach the nanometer scale, their behavior becomes increasingly sensitive to boundary conditions. In perovskite oxide nanocapacitors, epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening are well-established control parameters. Then, while expected to contribute to the epitaxial stabilization of ferroelectric ultrathin films, the lattice-dynamical state of the electrodes has not been isolated as an independent tuning knob. Here we call this poorly explored coupling interfacial phonon bias, whereby the electrodes' phonon energy landscape reshapes that of the adjacent ferroelectric across their shared interface. Using first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular-dynamics simulations, we examine this mechanism in symmetric BiFeO${}_3$ nanocapacitors in contact with a metallic perovskite oxide. By independently controlling the orientatio and amplitude of the electrodes' octahedral-tilt landscape, while keeping conventional elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed, we show that the electrodes' phonon energy landscape can modify the stability of competing BiFeO${}_3$ phases. In particular, this allows us to shift the ferroelectric transition temperature and even induce antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions. We thus showcase interfacial phonon bias as a complementary and powerful strategy to modify and optimize the properties of ultrathin epitaxial films.

title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
summary: The non-asymptotic flatness of charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the horizon electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics automatically satisfied, but also both the CR relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.

title: Theory of spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy with topological insulator tips
summary: Topological insulators have enabled a new class of spin-sensitive scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probes based on helical boundary states. However, how these probes generate a net spin-polarized tunneling current remains unclear. We present a theory of spin-polarized STM with topological insulator tips and show that asymmetric tunneling-contact geometry and spin dephasing enable helical boundary states to generate a spin-polarized tunneling current. Within the standard Landauer-Büttiker formalism, we demonstrate this mechanism for a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator tip: asymmetric contacts make the two counter-propagating helical edge states, which carry opposite spins, traverse path lengths that differ by $ΔL$, and spin dephasing induces backscattering that reduces the conductance more strongly for the longer path. For a representative asymmetric contact and weak spin dephasing, the QSH tip exhibits a tunneling spin polarization of $P_s=-17.2\%$ under positive bias, whose magnitude can reach $50\%$ for larger $ΔL$, and which remains robust against Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Crucially, this polarization, dominated by helical edge transport rather than by bulk states, naturally reverses sign with the bias polarity owing to spin-momentum locking. Our findings are consistent with recent STM experiments using topological tips.

title: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
summary: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $β=d\ln m/dφ$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $β_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $β_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|β|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $β_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.

title: A possible signature of neutrino spin precession in the J-PARC muon $g-2$ experiment
summary: We examine a possible signature of the neutrino angular-momentum contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly measurement in the J-PARC E34 experiment. In previous papers we argued that the angular momentum carried by the unobserved neutrino pair may leave an uncertainty in the anomaly inferred from the time modulation of detected positrons. At Fermilab the highly relativistic muons make the forward-emission approximation suitable for this estimate. The lower muon momentum at J-PARC requires the decay kinematics to be treated explicitly. We integrate the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the positron energy distribution and asymmetry derived from the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, and the same event-counting weight $N(E)A(E)$ is employed for both experiments. For positron energies between $1.5$ and $2.9$ GeV at Fermilab and between $200$ and $275$ MeV at J-PARC, the proposed correction is smaller at J-PARC by $0.415\pm0.176$ ppm, when the most optimistic E34 precision is assumed. The expected difference amounts to $2.36$ standard deviations if the future measurement is centred on this value. The calculation thus identifies an experimental comparison which may test the proposed effect independently of the hadronic contribution to the Standard Model prediction. We also examine the possibility of testing the effect by comparing measurements at two different muon momenta. With a fixed positron energy threshold of 200 MeV, the maximum sensitivity is obtained at a muon beam energy of 245 MeV. The predicted difference relative to the nominal J-PARC configuration has significance of $4.88σ$ for the most optimistic experimental sensitivity.

title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
summary: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $μ$-Distortion Constraints
summary: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $μ$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $μ$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.

title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
summary: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $ξ=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $ΔN_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.

title: Strain Controlled Hydrogen Interstitial Site Preference and Hydride Phase Suppression in Epitaxial Vanadium
summary: Understanding hydrogen behavior in transition metals is crucial for energy storage and sensing technologies. Here we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with in-situ electrical measurements to reveal how epitaxial strain governs hydrogen interstitial site selection and phase stability in vanadium. Our calculations demonstrate a robust thermodynamic preference for tetrahedral (T) over octahedral (O) sites, with the energy difference modulated by lattice anisotropy through strain-tunable H 1s-V 3d orbital hybridization. Experimentally, epitaxial V films on MgO(001) exhibit a critical thickness-dependent crossover: 50 nm films show characteristic first-order alpha-beta hydride transitions, while 10 nm films display continuous solid-solution behavior with complete transition suppression. This crossover is governed by the progressive relaxation of epitaxial strain with increasing film thickness: the 10 nm films retain strong coherent strain that flattens the free-energy landscape and suppresses hydride nucleation, whereas the 50 nm films approach the strain-relaxed bulk limit where long-range elastic interactions restore first-order phase behavior. Finite-size truncation of elastic fields and interfacial electronic reconstruction further reinforce this dimensional crossover. Our work establishes a unified framework connecting atomic-scale orbital physics to mesoscopic phase thermodynamics, providing design principles for strain-engineered metal-hydride systems.

title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
summary: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

title: A Rule That's Made to be Broken? Reframing the Arrhenius Law for Ionic Transport
summary: The Arrhenius law is ubiquitous in the physical sciences. It describes how an observable property scales with temperature, $T$, as $\exp(\pm E_A/k_BT)$ for a constant $E_A$, the 'activation energy'. Fitting to the Arrhenius law is a common procedure for both experimental and computational data. However, the physical significance of any 'activation energy' calculated is unclear. Here we focus on self-diffusion coefficients for potential solid electrolytes, and by identifying the individual 'diffusive steps' within the system, show how a physically significant activation energy can be extracted. There are also many examples of non-Arrhenius behaviour including `super-Arrhenius' curvature, where the effective activation energy appears to increase with decreasing temperature. We demonstrate how it is still possible to extract the underlying Arrhenius law, by quantifying self-correlations such as back-and-forth motion. The methodology described here is material-agnostic and can be utilised to analyse the molecular dynamics trajectories of both ordered and disordered materials.

title: sdos: spectral densities of large sparse Hermitian and generalized eigenproblems
comment: This is a software package for the highly efficient computation of densities of states for large Hermitian matrices. This is the companion paper to the github project (all described in manuscript)
summary: sdos is an open Python package that computes the density of states (DOS) and related spectral quantities of very large sparse Hermitian matrices A, and of generalized problems A psi = lambda B psi, from Chebyshev moments estimated with random vectors. The density is reconstructed by the kernel polynomial method (KPM, the default) or by maximum entropy (Maxent); the same interface gives band energies, Fermi levels, local and projected densities, harmonic thermodynamics, exact HOMO-LUMO gaps and eigenpairs in a spectral window. Interfaces cover electronic (empirical tight-binding, DFTB, SIESTA) and vibrational (matrix-free LAMMPS Hessians) problems. I checked most ingredients against dense diagonalization or an independent code; the exceptions are listed in Sec. V. On a workstation (4 threads, 19 GB) the DOS of an 884,736-atom amorphous silicon model (a 6^3 tiling of a 4096-atom cell; 3.5 million orbitals; the orthogonal empirical tight-binding model of Kwon et al.) takes 71 s (M=100, R=2, no exact moments; 383 s with the default exact moments), and a matrix-free 2,097,152-atom crystal 10 min in 1.8 GB. A 17^3 replica of a 216-atom amorphous cell (1,061,208 atoms) agrees with exact Bloch spectra: electronic DOS in 229 s, matrix-free ACE vibrational DOS in 2.2 h on one GPU. Shift-invert, incomplete-Cholesky setup, exact moments of high order and Maxent at high moment counts do not scale. The underlying methods are due to Silver, Roder, Kress, Voter, Drabold, Sankey and collaborators; the Introduction states what is added.

title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
summary: Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.

title: Visualizing d-wave pairing symmetry at the atomic scale in a cuprate high-Tc superconductor by Josephson tunneling
summary: Superconducting pairing symmetry provides crucial insight into the microscopic mechanisms of Cooper pairing. However, probing the local manifestations of sign-changing superconducting order parameters remains experimentally challenging. Here, we investigate the superconducting condensate in optimally doped (OPT) Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi-2223) using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), equipped with an s-wave superconducting tip. Measurements at ultra-low temperatures reveal a pronounced modulation of the Josephson tunneling signal at different locations inside the crystallographic unit cell. A distinct Josephson tunneling signal is detected above O sites in the underlying CuO2 plane, whereas the signal nearly vanishes above the Cu-plaquette diagonals, including Cu sites and plaquette centers. This unique intra-unit-cell spatial pattern agrees with the theoretical prediction for the symmetry-dependent cancellation of Josephson tunneling between an s-wave superconducting tip and a d-wave superconducting sample. Our findings provide atomic-scale, real-space evidence for d-wave pairing symmetry in OPT high-Tc Bi-2223 and establish SJTM as a powerful approach for investigating the pairing symmetry of unconventional superconductors.

title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
summary: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the Müger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
summary: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the $1$-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium

title: Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
summary: We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation.
